blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
[]{#sec1 label="sec1"}

In this paper we construct an invariant of integral homology spheres which unifies the $SU(2)$ Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants at all roots of unity, which we announced in a previous paper [@H:rims2001].

blocks.title: Surgery along a knot with framing $1/m$
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:surgery-along-knot label="sec:surgery-along-knot"}

Kirby and Melvin proved periodicity results for the WRT invariant of integral homology spheres obtained from $S^3$ by surgery along a knot with framings $1/m$ (Corollaries 8.15 and 8.26 of [@Kirby-Melvin]). We have the following generalization.

::: theorem
[]{#r9 label="r9"} Let $K$ be a knot in an integral homology sphere $M$. Let $M'=M_{K;1/m}$ be the result of surgery from $M$ along $K$ with framing $1/m$ with $m\in \modZ$. Then we have $$J_{M'}\equiv J_M \pmod{(q^{2m}-1)}.$$
:::

In this section, we give some remarks and discussions.

blocks.title: The WRT invariants as limiting values of holomorphic functions
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:wrt-invariants-as label="sec:wrt-invariants-as"} As explained in the introduction, the invariant $J_M$ for an integral homology sphere $M$ unifies the WRT invariants $\tau _\zeta (M)$ for all the roots of unity in an algebraic way. It should be remarked that there is another *analytic* approach to "unify" the WRT invariants by realizing the radial limiting values of a holomorphic function defined on the unit disk $\{z\in \C;\;|z|<1\}$, studied in [@Lawrence:integrality; @Lawrence:holomorphic; @Lawrence-Rozansky; @Lawrence-Zagier; @Hikami1; @Hikami3; @Hikami4; @Hikami5].

blocks.title: Generalizations to simple Lie algebra
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:general label="sec:general"}

In a joint work with Le [@H-Le:in-preparation], for each simple Lie algebra $\g$, we will generalize the invariant $J_M\in \Zqh$ of integral homology sphere $M$ to an invariant $J^\g_M\in \Zqh$. This invariant can be characterized by the property that for each root of unity $\zeta$ such that the quantum $\g$ invariant $\tau ^\g_M$ is well-defined, we have $\mods _\zeta (J^\g_M)=\tau ^\g_\zeta$. This specialization property holds also for the projective quantum $\g$ invariant. See [@Ohtsuki5 Conjecture 7.29] for a precise statement.
